answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition mass discounted at each step. A sybil cluster behaves like an island: few honest attestations create a sparse external cut and low conductance, so min-cut transitivity bounds limit the probability that walks enter and remain there. Thus its aggregate voting weight is mathematically capped, even if internal links multiply like a comet or branch through karst.
